title: Anima vs. QuantumLoopAI (EMMA): AI reception for GP practices
summary: Anima vs. QuantumLoopAI’s EMMA for NHS GP practices: compare AI telephone reception, request capture and workflow handoff, with FAQs on switching.
body_markdown:
## What is an AI receptionist?


AI telephone reception helps GP practices collect patient requests over the phone and pass them to the team responsible for responding. Patients need to get through, explain what they need and reach a person when necessary. Reception teams need clear information they can act on, including when a call is incomplete or needs attention.


Anima, QuantumLoopAI’s EMMA, X-on Health Voice Agent and InTouchNow AI handle patient calls using AI. Answering the phone is the first step. Your team then needs a clear request it can act on. Here’s how Anima and EMMA connect those steps.

## FAQs


### What should you test in an AI receptionist demonstration?


Try routine administrative requests, callers who change their mind and callers who ask to speak to reception. Test background noise, pauses and the languages relevant to your patient population. Ask how incomplete calls are recorded, how staff identify requests needing attention and what happens if the telephone or consultation system is unavailable.


### Does answering the call complete the request?


Call answering and request resolution are separate stages. Follow a test call through to the staff inbox and check whether the team receives the information needed to act. Establish who owns the request, how the patient receives a response and how duplicate requests are handled. Ask suppliers to demonstrate escalation and human handoff rather than inferring these capabilities from the term AI receptionist.


### How should you compare AI reception costs and implementation?


Ask about call-volume charges, telephone integration, workflow configuration, staff training and ongoing support. Agree a way to assess call completion, the quality of captured information and the workload left for reception. Keep existing patient access routes available while the practice evaluates a new telephone workflow.


## Are you planning a change in telephone reception?


Start with your call volumes, existing telephony and the work your reception team handles. Agree how patients will reach staff and how requests will enter the practice workflow.
